Two trips are armed only while reacting

SIFArmedLatchedReset

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • The SRS follows LOPA and precedes the logic.
  • Three SIFs share one short-stop, XV-104.
  • Safe state: reaction killed, charges shut, cooling forced.
  • XS-101 and FSLL-110 are armed only while reacting.

Part 2 · Fast enough?

Is each trip fast enough for the time the reactor allows?

Part 2 · the plan

Two clocks: the reactor and the trip

  1. Process safety timetrip point to hazard, from the model
  2. Response timesensor, logic, delay, valve stroke
  3. The race on the modelwhat R-101 does when the trip is late
  4. Fast but wrongSIF-4 acts on a valve that cannot help

Definitions

The trip must finish well inside the PST

Part 1 said what each trip does; now: how fast it must do it.

$t_{trip}$
time the variable crosses the trip point
s
$t_{haz}$
time the hazard begins with no SIF action
s
$PST$
process safety time
s
$t_{resp}$
SIF response time
s
$t_{delay},\ t_{stroke}$
trip delay set in the logic; valve stroke time
s
$PST=t_{haz}-t_{trip}$measured on the model with the trips disabled
$t_{resp}=0.5+0.25+t_{delay}+t_{stroke}$sensor, logic scan, delay, valve (2 s assumed)
$t_{resp}\le PST/2$good practice; Check up to PST, Gap beyond

Where each clock stops

The hazard is the PSV-100 set point

SIFDemand in the runTrip pointHazard reached?
SIF-1CW supply −95 % at 2.0 hTI-101 > 63 °C15 bar g
SIF-2agitator stops at 4.0 hmotor stoppedno
SIF-3P-101A stops at 4.0 h< 120 m³/hno
SIF-4FV-103 passinglevel > 94 %15 bar g

The lumped, well-mixed model cannot show a separated layer.

Interactive · set the delay and the valve stroke

Response time against the process safety time

Two clocks$t_{resp}=0.75+t_{delay}+t_{stroke}\ \le PST/2$

SIF-1 has about 15 min against 12.75 s: on R-101 time is not the weak point.

Interactive · the R-101 model with a late short-stop

How high the pressure goes when the trip acts R seconds late

The PSV set is reached once R passes the PST: the margin is real reactor time.

Interactive · SIF-4 with FV-103 passing, whole SIS active

LSHH-100 acts in time, on the wrong valve

FIC-103 at 0 % cannot stop a passing FV-103; a block valve on the trip can.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • PST: trip point to PSV set, from the model.
  • SIF-1: about 15 min against 12.75 s.
  • SIF-2 and SIF-3: no PST from a well-mixed model.
  • SIF-4 is fast but needs a block valve.

Derivation · the needed PFD

Scenario frequency is linear in the SIF's PFD

A trip fast enough must also work when demanded.

$f$
scenario frequency, all causes
/yr
$a$
paths that bypass the SIF
/yr
$b$
demand rate reaching the SIF
/yr
$f_{tgt}$
tolerable frequency for the severity
/yr
$f=a+b\cdot PFD_{SIF}$every path through the SIF scales with its PFD
$PFD_{need}=\dfrac{f_{tgt}-a}{b}$set the scenario frequency equal to the target
$a\ge f_{tgt}\Rightarrow$ no $PFD_{need}$other paths alone already exceed the target

Interactive · pick a LOPA scenario

Where the line crosses the target is the PFD needed

Previous slide$f=a+b\cdot PFD_{SIF}$

In L3, power failure bypasses the SIF: no PFD of XS-101 alone meets the target.

Given · low-demand PFD

The achieved PFD adds up subsystem by subsystem

$\lambda_{DU}$
dangerous undetected failure rate of one channel
/yr
$T$
proof-test interval
yr
$PFD_{avg}$
average probability of failure on demand
–
$PFD_{avg}\approx\sum_{sub}\lambda_{DU}T/2$1oo1 subsystems in series, valid while $\lambda T\ll 1$
$1oo2:\ (\lambda_{DU}T)^2/3$either of two channels can act
$RRF=1/PFD_{avg}$risk reduction factor of the SIF

Which component sets each trip's PFD?

Previous slide$PFD_{avg}\approx\sum\lambda_{DU}T/2$

A second sensor changes little; the short-stop hardware sets the PFD.

Common cause in the SRS

Fix the shared final element once, for all four

One credit

L4: TSHH-101 is not a second layer behind FSLL-110.

Air to open

XV-104 needs instrument air: air loss is common cause (R39).

SIL 2 short-stop

PT-105 permissive, XV-104B, air receiver: 2.7×10⁻³.

Interactive · accept recommendations

Each gap closes with a named change

L1 closes with the short-stop or the relief; L3 and L4 need relief plus a new SIF.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • Needed PFD: where $f=a+b\cdot PFD$ meets the target.
  • SIF-1 gives 2.5×10⁻², needs 2.0×10⁻²: Gap.
  • XV-104, pot and line carry 98 % of it.
  • L3 and L4 close only with relief and new SIFs.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Write the SRS from the LOPA result before building any logic.

2

Name every final element's position in the safe state.

3

Measure the PST on the model; keep the response under half.

4

Check that the trip acts on a valve that removes the cause.

5

Verify the PFD against what the scenario needs, final element first.
